description:
Add one activeness predicate on `Lease` and three lock-free lease reads in storage, and move every command that reads leases without the claims lock onto them.

## Background

Lease activeness is decided by different rules: `ClaimsIndex::conflicting_lease` (`crates/jit/src/storage/claim_coordinator.rs`, not expired and not stale), `Lease::is_expired`, `commands/worktree.rs` (expiry only) and `commands/validate.rs` (its own expiry comparison, reporting expired and orphaned leases, so it needs every stored lease). `Lease::is_stale` exists. Lock-free readers load the whole index through `ClaimsIndex::load`: `refuse_foreign_leases_read` (`commands/mod.rs`), the `worktree list` claim counts (`commands/worktree.rs`, whose unit tests build a `ClaimsIndex` by hand), and `validate --leases` (`commands/validate.rs`).

`validate_claims_index_with_paths` (`commands/validate.rs`) is not a lease reader: it checks the index file itself, and it leaves when the index does.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `Lease::is_active(now)` is true when a lease is neither expired nor stale, one unit test owns its boundaries, and `conflicting_lease` decides activeness through it.
- [hard] REQ-02: `storage/claim_coordinator.rs` offers `read_leases(&WorktreePaths)` (every stored lease), `read_active_leases(&WorktreePaths, now)` and `read_active_lease(&WorktreePaths, &IssueId, now)`, reading without the claims lock, with unit tests.
- [hard] REQ-03: `validate --leases` reads through `read_leases`; `refuse_foreign_leases_read` and `worktree list` read through the active reads. No lease reader outside the coordinator calls `ClaimsIndex::load`, and no command compares a lease's expiry or heartbeat itself.
- [hard] REQ-04: The worktree unit tests build leases without a `ClaimsIndex`, and the lease-validation CLI tests pass unchanged. `worktree list` counts a stale lease as inactive.
title: Lock-free lease readers use the storage read path
